additions.reason: The Torah explicitly identifies מַלְכוּת דַּעֲשִׂיָּה as the bechina of faith in the context of commerce: 'וּמַלְכוּת דַּעֲשִׂיָּה, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינוֹת הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁבַּמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן.' Malkhut of Asiyah IS the bechina of faith — they share the same essential nature (receptive, faithful presence, rising from the klipot). This node belongs in Package 3 (אמונה/ירושלים) because its essential quality is identical to אמונה — not eitza (it does not 'produce' faith; it IS faith at the level of Asiyah).
additions.source_quote: וּמַלְכוּת דַּעֲשִׂיָּה, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינוֹת הָאֱמוּנָה שֶׁבַּמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן כַּנַּ"ל, עוֹלָה מִן הַקְּלִפּוֹת

additions.reason: The verse fragment 'וּנְתָנוֹ ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶיךָ' (Devarim 21:10 — 'and Hashem your God will give him into your hands') is explicitly identified as a bechina of אמונה via the proof-verse 'וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה' (Shemot 17:12 — 'and his hands were faithfulness/emunah'). 'Into your hands' = the hands of faith = faith itself. This belongs in Package 3 alongside the other faith-expressions. The hands are synonymous with the bechina of faith that raises the sparks.
additions.source_quote: וּנְתָנוֹ ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּיָדֶיךָ – זֶה בְּחִינַת אֱמוּנָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה

additions.reason: The Torah explicitly says: 'זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת פְּנִימִיּוּת הַמֹּחִין דַּעֲשִׂיָּה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁל הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן' — the inner thought during commerce is the bechina of the inner mind of Asiyah. This is the pnimiyut of the commerce domain (Package 1), expressly equated with חַבַּ
additions.source_quote: זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת פְּנִימִיּוּת הַמֹּחִין דַּעֲשִׂיָּה, הַיְנוּ שֶׁל הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינוֹת עֲשִׂיָּה

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: דין תורה (as a bechina of Torah — the Torah implicitly calls litigation 'Torah returning to its source', but this is more narrative/eitza than explicit bechina language)
analysis_notes.coverage_notes: All 17 nodes from the 12 bechina edges are assigned to exactly one package. The dataset captures the three main thematic axes well: commerce/sparks (Package 1), Torah/Formation (Package 2), and faith/Jerusalem (Package 3). The largest gap is מלכות דעשיה, which the text explicitly identifies as bechina of אמונה and is the technical counterpart to חבד דעשיה (which rises to יצירה). Adding it to Package 3 would complete the Kabbalistic structural pair described in line 10-11 of the source text.
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_note: Torah #280 is predominantly positive — it discusses how commerce and faith work together to raise sparks and serve Torah. There is no explicit evil package. The Torah mentions those who 'uproot commerce from Torah' (עוֹקֵר הַמַּשָּׂא וּמַתָּן מִן הַתּוֹרָה) as sinners who receive punishment, but no evil conceptual cluster is built with bechina language. The klipot appear as a context/setting (the sparks fall into them), not as a developed thematic package.
